articles.title: India bonds give up marginal opening gains as profit booking takes over
articles.desc: Indian government bonds fell after initial gains due to profit booking by traders and a sharp rupee decline. The benchmark yield of the 6.94% 2036 bond increased to 7.2185% during trading hours. Last week, the yield had dropped significantly due to lower US Treasury yields and a stronger rupee. Investors now focus on the upcoming Reserve Bank of India's policy decision on December 4.

articles.title: Rupee retreats, Goldman calls it a 'port of stability' in AI storm
articles.desc: The Indian rupee initially rose to a seven-month high before retreating amid corporate dollar buying. It is on track for a monthly gain of over 2%, bolstered by significant foreign investment in Indian equities. Analysts noted that the rupee's early gains pushed it into overbought territory, prompting some selling. Despite recent fluctuations, the rupee has remained stable compared to other major currencies.

articles.title: The great Indian stock market comeback. Can the rally sustain and what should investors do?
articles.desc: Indian equities staged a sharp 9.7% rally in eight sessions through November 12, reversing months of underperformance. A sell-off in US AI stocks, triggered by Republican losses in the midterm elections and fears of tighter AI regulation, spilled across global technology markets. Earlier, foreign investor outflows, elevated crude prices and rupee weakness had weighed heavily on Dalal Street sentiment.

articles.title: India factory demand offsets weaker services growth in November, PMI shows
articles.desc: India's private sector activity experienced marginal growth in November, driven by manufacturing demand and production. The HSBC Flash India Composite Purchasing Managers' Index rose slightly from October, indicating continued expansion. The manufacturing sector achieved a nine-month high, while the services sector saw a decline in growth. Employment trends diverged, with factories increasing hiring and services sectors reducing jobs. Companies exhibited optimism about future performance, although confidence remained below historic averages.

articles.title: South Korean shares slump nearly 3% on AI-driven tech selloff despite policy pledge
articles.desc: South Korean shares fell approximately 3% on Monday amid government efforts to stabilize the market. The KOSPI index dropped to its lowest level since January, raising investor concerns. Major technology stocks, including Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, experienced significant losses during this decline. Authorities pledged to use stabilization funds but faced skepticism from investors regarding future returns. This situation reflects broader doubts about AI investments affecting global technology stocks.

Following recent market volatility, prospects for a significant rate hike in December appear less likely. Meanwhile, cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin and Ether, have seen slight downturns.

Continued investment in infrastructure aims to support future growth and prevent slippage back into poverty. Achieving Viksit Bharat by 2047 remains a shared goal for India's development.

articles.title: Asia, Africa to drive expansion of India's export markets as shipments grow across regions
articles.desc: India's merchandise exports have shown strong growth, particularly in Africa and Asia, according to recent government data. Exports to Africa increased by 44 percent, while shipments to Asia surpassed USD 100 billion. Engineering goods, electronic goods, and petroleum products have driven this expansion significantly. Notable growth was observed in markets such as Tanzania and Kenya in Africa.

articles.title: South Korea prepares market stabilisation funds after KOSPI hits 10-month low
articles.desc: In response to falling stock indices, South Korea's finance ministry is poised to activate market stabilisation funds. The KOSPI index has plummeted, marking its lowest point in the last ten months. An emergency meeting was convened by the finance minister to explore strategies for restoring investor confidence. Among the discussed actions are temporary regulations on stock buyback limits for publicly listed companies.

articles.title: Chinese national Li Ming charged in fraud case in Singapore linked to Megaspeed and Alice Huang: Report
articles.desc: Li Ming, a Chinese national, is facing fraud charges in Singapore regarding alleged transshipment of Nvidia chips. He was involved with Megaspeed, a company linked to Alice Huang, the former romantic partner of Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang. Li is accused of misleading an American supplier by misrepresenting the intended destination of purchased servers. Following an investigation, Megaspeed was placed on a no sell list by Nvidia.

articles.title: Crude oil futures brace for OPEC+ output decision amid supply glut concerns: Analysts

Traders are keeping a close eye on supply insights from the American Petroleum Institute and Energy Information Administration. Trading will be quiet on Tuesday due to Guru Nanak Jayanti. While concerns about a global supply surplus loom large, they overshadow geopolitical tensions in West Asia.
